sameDayRetelling: My 7th heir, Iris, walked straight down to the Mirror King at D33 carrying the rules I had written after the last two deaths. I had just added a shield bash on telegraphs, and when the King mirrored her down to 23 of 52 she drank a heal, bashed, and the King fell. She walked on to D34 and the game told me the dungeon was cleared after 23 runs and 6 deaths.

axes.proxy: time-to-first-rule-edit; misread rate on the trace
axes.note: Forecast deltas and death traces are clear ('VS LAST RUN · full haul 13→50%'), but copy misled me several times: pen lock 'Custom rules / Upcoming reports', tip 'custom rules · write hero rules · unlocks later' shown after I owned 5 rules, tactics 'change' toggles a chooser closed, compare 'noise · 8 runs'.

Real foreseeable trade-offs: Guarded 'better 8/8', corridor fighting 'worse 7/8', threshold sweep on my telegraph rule (hp<40% death 50%, hp<10% 13%), shield bash vs drink heal ($3075 vs $1368/run). Lapse: forge/legacy/worker buys are a strictly-ordered 'buy everything' chore.

I learned captives are worth freeing and telegraphs want a bash; but much growth was the apprentice forging ('forge −$20925') rather than my skill, and hunger ('starving −56') stayed a wall I never learned to answer.
King fights sweated ('KING MIRRORS' to 2/50 hp, 'Carried $4291 · Secured $0'); but most of each run is pre-resolved in a 'D1–32 · 100% · +$3228' summary chip, so stakes live in the last floors only.

axes.note: 'Cut the captive down. The stairs are clear.' changed my rules; nest wakes, iron golem 'REFLECTED!', gas, Lich summons. But fens hunger/drain repeated run after run ('hunger −26 max', '−30', '−56').

Five rules of my own (captives, drain, telegraph bash, low-hp unknown scroll) — recognisably mine; but they sit on top of 7+ package rows I did not author and the custom row is pinned at the top (step-down disabled).

Heir 1 killed by 'Krusk the slag crawler', heir 2 report 'avenged Krusk', 7th heir 'MIRROR KING DOWN' after my bash rule. Lapse: offline runs collapse to one-line ledger entries ('died $0 · to gas'), so 4 of 6 deaths had no told story.
